rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent stepped compact mass in all four views, with a single dominant gesture and no obvious cross-view collision, so the basic massing is stable. However, the program contract demands a neighborhood-living building with an active ground threshold and a meaningful public void/court responding to the access edge. Here the form is mostly a sealed, terraced block with only a shallow ground response; the blue frontage edge is not met by a clearly legible public void, entry seam, or undercut. The silhouette is acceptable as an early-stage landform, but the sectional logic does not yet support the required active street relationship or a convincing mixed-use public threshold. References 3–4 support the idea of a voided, overhung, compact mass; reference 5 supports terrace logic, but the candidate still needs a stronger carved public ground condition and access-side articulation.
